stimulus.source_note: John Brown, note written on the morning of his execution, December 2, 1859. Public domain.
stimulus.text: I, John Brown, am now quite certain that the crimes of this guilty land will never be purged away but with blood. I had, as I now think, vainly flattered myself that without very much bloodshed it might be done.

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note

rationales.A: Background from the books: California was already a state by 1859; Brown’s raid struck a federal armory in Virginia, not the West.
rationales.B: Brown fought slavery, not for it; his raid aimed to arm enslaved people, the opposite of defending the law that returned them.
rationales.C: Background from the books: Brown was not a candidate and sought no office; his plan was an armed uprising, not an election.
rationales.D: Brown captured the armory at Harpers Ferry to hand its weapons to enslaved people, hoping to begin a rebellion that would break slavery.
rationales.general:
1. Place Brown at Harpers Ferry: he seized a federal armory in Virginia in 1859.
2. Background from the books: he meant to give the armory’s weapons to enslaved people and start a rebellion.
3. Read his last note through that plan: blood, he now believes, is the only price that will purge the land.
Remember: a last note explains a life’s plan; read the raid through the words written after it.
